settings.aboutBody: Snatchy is a local-first weightlifting technique tool. It analyses a lift on your own device using body-pose estimation, so your video never leaves your phone or browser.
settings.privacyNote: No account, no server, no upload. Everything you record stays on this device.
settings.authorBody: Snatchy is built and maintained by Fede Lochbaum, an engineer and lifelong lifter who wanted a tool that explains the movement instead of just rating it.
settings.supportBody: Snatchy is free, has no ads and no tracking. If it helped you understand a lift, a coffee keeps the model downloads and the work going.
settings.supportIssuesHint: Found a bug or a bad translation? Open an issue.
settings.creator: Fede Lochbaum

checkDetail.armsThroughPull: Minimum visible elbow angle over the recognized pull interval. Unrecognized portions of the pull are excluded.
checkDetail.hipExtension: Hip angle at the measured end of the recognized pull.
checkDetail.kneeExtension: Knee angle at the measured end of the recognized pull.
checkDetail.frontRackFlexion: Elbow flexion (180° minus elbow angle) at the estimated front rack. This checks a receiving-position cue, not shoulder contact or competition validity.
checkDetail.receivingArmExtension: Visible elbow angle at the estimated catch. Inspect the overlay before interpreting a shortfall as a fault.
checkDetail.standingRecovery: Knee angle in the recognized receiving-position recovery. This does not establish a competition-valid lift.

checksPanel.title: The details that matter
checksPanel.tipReview: Review this moment in the video overlay to inspect joint alignment.
checksPanel.reviewTiming: Inspect surrounding phase timing and wrist path.
checksPanel.reviewAlignment: Check the joint overlay against the actual limb position.
checksPanel.noneScored: No technique score assigned. No recognized phase has enough reliable evidence for a measurement check. Try a steady side view with the whole athlete visible.
checksPanel.formulaHead: Score = checks met ÷ available checks × 100. Missing checks are excluded, not failed. Up to five visible-angle checks are assessed: pull elbow ≥160°, end-of-pull hip and knee ≥165°,
checksPanel.formulaDisclaimer: These are transparent prototype rules, not validated coaching standards.
checksPanel.partialCounts: {resolved} of {applicable} phases recognized · {available} of 5 checks available.
checksPanel.partialNoMissing: Some recognized phases lack enough evidence for their measurement checks.
checksPanel.partialDisclaimer: Score uses available checks only. Missing phases are not penalized. Even 100/100 is not a complete assessment or a measure of accuracy.
checksPanel.summaryNoScore: Body landmarks measured from your video. More phase evidence is needed for a movement score.
checksPanel.summaryOne: {count} measured check needs review. Start with {check} ({value}{unit}).
checksPanel.summaryMany: {count} measured checks need review. Start with {check} ({value}{unit}).
checksPanel.summaryAll: All {count} measured angle checks met their thresholds. Review the phases and bar path for the full picture.

radarPanel.footnote: Extension is the upper measured angle; excursion is the difference between the lower and upper angles. All axes use 0–180°, based on the 5th–95th percentile ranges.
radarPanel.improveRecording: Improve the recording first: use a steady side view, good lighting, and keep the whole athlete visible.
radarPanel.noneEstablished: No technique improvement was established by these measurements. Review the timestamped moments below with a coach; the chart shows motion, not an ideal target.
radarPanel.title: Movement profile
radarPanel.lede: Your measured angles at a glance. A larger shape does not mean better technique.
radarPanel.chartAria: Five-axis radar chart of measured joint angles, zero to 180 degrees.

eventDetails.extension: Projected hip angle {angle}°. This is a measured image-plane angle, not proof of full extension.
eventDetails.knee-flexion: Projected knee angle {angle}°. Inspect this frame to locate the receiving position.
eventDetails.elbow-flexion: Projected elbow angle {angle}°. Occlusion and camera perspective can affect this estimate.
eventDetails.overhead: The visible wrist stays above the shoulder with an extended elbow for three samples. This alone does not verify an overhead catch or a Snatch.
eventDetails.possible-early-bend: Elbow flexion was visible approximately {ms} ms before the largest observed hip angle. Experimental rule; review the frames before changing technique.

barTrack.title: Track your bar
barTrack.intro: Pause just before the lift. Mark the center of the visible plate, then its outer edge. Enter the actual plate diameter. Use a fixed side-view camera; the plate must remain in the same plane.
barTrack.canvasAria: Video frame for plate selection. Click center then edge, or use the position fields below.
barTrack.stationary: The camera is stationary and the plate stays in the same plane.
barTrack.reviewIntro: Scrub through the tracked interval. The highlighted dot must stay on the plate center. Reject and retrack if it follows the background or another object.
barTrack.verified: I reviewed the tracked interval and the dot follows the plate.
barTrack.prefilled: Automatic candidate prefilled. Verify the marked plate and enter its measured diameter.
barTrack.markCenter: Mark the plate center, then its outer edge.
barTrack.markEdge: Now mark the outer edge of this plate.
barTrack.enterDiameter: Enter the real diameter and confirm the camera setup.
barTrack.failed: Bar tracking failed. Please try again.

phaseEvidence.transitionUnresolved: No distinct knee rebend was resolved. It may be obscured by the view or absent as a separate phase in this variation.
phaseEvidence.unresolved: Not resolved from the available pose evidence.
phaseEvidence.highHangInapplicable: Not applicable to a high-hang start. Analysis begins with the upper pull.
phaseEvidence.highHangNoFloorPull: Not applicable to a high-hang start; no floor-to-knee first pull is assumed.
phaseEvidence.highHangUpperPull: Upper-pull onset from the selected high-hang starting position.
phaseEvidence.setup: Hands below hips with flexed knees or a hip hinge before upward movement. A hang start is allowed; floor contact is not established.
phaseEvidence.firstPull: Wrist rises from the starting position for three observed samples. Lift-off is a pose estimate, not bar contact detection.
phaseEvidence.catchRack: Hands near shoulders with flexed elbows for three observed samples. Estimated front-rack receiving position.
phaseEvidence.catchOverhead: Extended arm above shoulder for three samples with flexed knees. Estimated receiving position.
phaseEvidence.turnover: Largest combined hip/knee extension before the receiving position.
phaseEvidence.transition: First local knee-extension peak before a measurable knee rebend.
phaseEvidence.secondPull: Knee rebend minimum followed by renewed extension.
phaseEvidence.secondPullEstimated: Timing estimate: hands approach hip level during measured hip extension before turnover. A separate knee rebend was not resolved; this is not a bar-contact measurement.
phaseEvidence.recoveryRack: Standing recovery while the hands remain in the front-rack region.
phaseEvidence.recoveryOverhead: Knees extend from the receiving position while the arm remains overhead.
phaseEvidence.partialCoverage: Some joint measurements are unavailable in this interval; timing uses the remaining observed samples.

snatch-pull.instruction: Practice the first and second pull without catching. Keep your arms long as your legs and hips finish extending.
snatch-pull.cue: Push through the floor. Finish tall.

tall-snatch.instruction: Start standing tall with an empty or light bar. Pull yourself under and receive in a stable overhead squat.

high-hang-snatch.instruction: Start with the bar at the upper thigh. Drive with your legs, finish extension, then move decisively under.

arms.what: The elbows bend visibly while the bar is still well below the hip, before the legs and hips have finished extending.
arms.why: Bending the arms early shortens the pull and usually sends the bar forward, so the athlete has to fight it back into position.
arms.how: Keep the arms long and let the legs and hips do the work. Think about pushing the floor away rather than pulling with the biceps.

drift.what: The bar travels forward of the body instead of staying close to the legs and hips.
drift.why: A forward path means the bar meets the body late, which pushes the athlete into a deeper, less stable receiving position.
drift.how: Pull the bar close to the legs and hips, and keep the lats engaged so the bar tracks straight up.

turnover.what: The bar takes longer to pass the hips and reach the shoulders than it should.
turnover.why: A slow turnover is usually a sign that extension was not finished, which costs height and can make the catch harder to stabilise.
turnover.how: Finish the leg and hip drive before turning the arms over, and keep the bar close while it passes the hips.

demoSummary.good: A strong foundation. Let’s refine the details.
